tech-news.headline: Claude Code v2.1.304 adds /auto-mode-setup, which teaches auto mode about your project from recent sessions.
tech-news.note: The Hacker News page for 2026-10-20 failed to load, so HN items come from the 2026-10-19 front page; Reddit was read through Composio.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.304 adds guided auto mode setup
items.body: Claude Code v2.1.304 adds /auto-mode-setup, a guided setup that reads your project and recent sessions to teach auto mode about your environment. It also adds /claude-api managed-agents-secure, which checks a Managed Agents agent against Anthropic's security guide without changes. Pro and Max users now get a warning when a resumed inactive conversation would use a large share of the 5-hour limit. Fixes include safety prompts for rm -r on mounted drives such as /mnt/c.
items.why: Auto mode can learn your repo and tooling, so daily agent runs need fewer permission prompts.

items.title: Claude inference hooks leave beta for Enterprise organizations
items.body: Anthropic moved inference hooks out of beta for Claude Enterprise on October 20. Anthropic sends a signed HTTPS POST with the transcript to your server, which returns allow or deny within a 5-second default timeout. One hook covers claude.ai, Cowork, Claude Code, Claude in Chrome and more, with shadow mode and rollout percentage for safe rollout. It is not available on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud or API-only organizations.
items.why: A security server can now allow or deny every Claude prompt and tool call before it runs, across all Claude products.

items.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, its production inference stack
items.body: DeepSeek released DeepInfer under Apache 2.0. It is the framework behind DeepSeek's production services and targets DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on NVIDIA SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs. Features include expert parallelism, DSpark speculative decoding, deterministic sampling and structured outputs. It does not include a KV cache system or prefill/decode disaggregation.
items.why: It shows how a frontier lab serves a large MoE model, with code you can run and study.

items.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash: cheap, fast agentic coding model
items.body: MiniMax released M3.1 Flash with claimed gains in coding, computer use and cybersecurity. It reports 73.7% on DeepSWE v1.1, 61.7 on OSWorld V2 and 200+ tokens per second output. Pricing is $0.15 input and $0.60 output per million tokens, and agentic task cost is 70% lower than the previous model. Weights are not released yet; access is through the MiniMax API and MiniMax Code.
items.why: A low-cost model option for sub-agents and bulk coding tasks at $0.15 per million input tokens.

items.title: OpenAI models jump on COBOL and Fortran coding
items.body: OpenAI introduced MultiLangBench, which tests building a SQLite-compatible engine in 20 languages. GPT-6 Astra scored 87.4% on average, up from 26.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol, with COBOL rising from 10.9% to 72.1%. On a COBOL migration eval, GPT-6.1 Sol reached 86.6% at low effort and 97.9% at higher effort. The eval setup and results are on GitHub.
items.why: Legacy migration is common client work, and OpenAI published an open benchmark you can reuse.

items.title: Tmux and Claude Code: running many agents, and the limits
items.body: The guide covers claude --worktree --tmux, one tmux session per repo, send-keys -l to script prompts, and capture-pane or pipe-pane to read agent output. It shows a status-line script that marks each agent as working, parked or idle. It lists limits: no agent state, no completion signal and brittle screen scraping. The author sells a competing product, so the comparison is not neutral.
items.why: Practical send-keys and capture-pane patterns for running parallel Claude Code agents on remote boxes.

items.title: Mistral releases Timestral time-series forecasting models
items.body: Mistral released Timestral in four sizes: 5M, 28M, 123M and 209M parameters, under a Modified MIT license. The 209M model ranks first among zero-shot models on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench. On an 8-thread CPU, a one-day forecast takes about 10 ms with the 5M model and 140 ms with the 209M model. Models are on GitHub and Hugging Face.
items.why: Small CPU-friendly forecasters can drive capacity planning and anomaly alerts in ops pipelines.

x-desk.headline: OpenAI says its latest models now build and migrate software in COBOL, Fortran and Visual Basic, and this post led AI engagement on X yesterday.
x-desk.note: Read 31 posts in 2 searches; 8 passed the value filter and the top 6 by engagement are listed.

items.title: OpenAI models improve at COBOL, Fortran and Visual Basic
items.body: OpenAI says its latest model advances give "stronger capabilities for building and migrating software in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic." OpenAI notes that banks, governments and businesses depend on software in these languages. The post links to more detail.
items.why: Legacy migration is a common enterprise modernisation job that often ends on AWS, so this is a new use for coding agents in client work.

items.title: Claude helps design protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins
items.body: Anthropic published a Science Blog post on protein binders designed against scorpion neurotoxins. Scorpions sting about 1.2 million people every year, and antivenoms are often costly or in short supply. Anthropic calls the work "an early step toward finding new treatments."
items.why: It shows how Anthropic applies Claude to long, multi-step science work, the same agentic pattern that agent builders use every day.

items.title: Gemini 4 Argon builds a 3D periodic table in Antigravity
items.body: Google DeepMind shows Gemini 4 Argon building a 3D periodic table synced to Tom Lehrer's song "The Elements." The app was made in Antigravity. It animates orbiting electrons, atomic data and light spectra.
items.why: It is a demo of the coding strength of a new Gemini model that competes with Claude Code for agentic coding.

items.title: OpenAI API adds 12-hour prompt caching
items.body: The OpenAI API now offers 12-hour prompt caching. Persistent agents can keep shared instructions, tools and context cached longer. They pay the lower cached-input rate "even when requests are hours apart."
items.why: Long cache lifetimes cut cost for long-running agents, so compare this with Claude prompt caching when you design agent workloads.

items.title: DeepSeek shares inference details for V4.1 Flash on Zhihu
items.body: swyx points to a DeepSeek Zhihu post with more detail than the English posts on X. DeepSeek says it used its framework to run "a high-throughput, low-latency large-scale inference service for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash." The post links to the source.
items.why: Large-scale inference design is useful input if you host open models on AWS for agents.

items.title: Meta publishes technical report on Muse Glimmer, a 30B open-weight agent model
items.body: Meta published a technical report on Muse Glimmer, a 30B open-weight model built for agentic tasks on consumer hardware. It runs at practical speeds on a Mac or PC with one consumer GPU at 4-bit precision. Meta says it leads comparably sized open models on tool use.
items.why: A small open model with strong tool use is a candidate for local or self-hosted agents where cost or data rules block hosted APIs.

gadgets.headline: Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, goes on sale October 23 with limited walk-in stock.
gadgets.note: The Verge blocked access, and the Apple Newsroom and Google blog index pages showed no dated articles.

items.title: iPhone Duo launches Friday with limited walk-in stock
items.body: Apple says Apple Stores will have limited iPhone Duo stock for walk-in customers at launch on Friday, October 23, due to strong pre-order demand. The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable iPhone, with a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display. It starts at $1,999 and uses Touch ID and a 48MP main camera. In India and nine other markets, store pickup requires an online reservation instead of a walk-in purchase.
items.why: Buyers who want Apple's first foldable on day one need a pre-order or reservation in many countries.

items.title: OPPO Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max go global
items.body: OPPO launched the Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max internationally on October 21, with sales open in the UK, Germany, France and other markets. Both use the 2nm MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro chip and have 7,150mAh batteries in Europe. The Pro Max has triple 200MP rear cameras. European prices are €1,400 (256GB) and €1,500 (512GB) for the Find X10 and €1,800 (512GB) for the Pro Max.
items.why: OPPO's 200MP camera flagships reach Europe now, with an India launch set for the next day.

items.title: Apple sets 'Pro and Tell' Mac and iPad event for October 28
items.body: Apple sent invitations for a 'Pro and Tell' press and creator briefing in Los Angeles on October 28. It is a hands-on experience, not a traditional keynote. Apple has not confirmed which products it will show. Reports expect an OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro, M6 Macs and an OLED iPad mini.
items.why: Buyers of Macs and the iPad mini may want to wait one week for new models.

items.title: Garmin launches Edge Explore 3 cycling computers from $399
items.body: Garmin announced the Edge Explore 3 at $399 and the Edge Explore 3 Plus at $499. They have a 3-inch display, 32GB storage, IPX7 water resistance and up to 48 hours of battery in battery saver mode. The Plus model adds a speaker and microphone for hands-free voice control and voice messages. Pre-orders open October 23 in North America and Oceania and November 3 in Europe.
items.why: Cyclists get a cheaper Garmin unit with double storage, up to 48 hours of battery and voice control.

items.title: Xbox chief puts next console at Holiday 2028, handheld 2027
items.body: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told Fortune that the next Xbox console is planned for Holiday 2028. She also named a next-generation handheld device for the 2027 holiday season. Microsoft has not confirmed device names, specs or prices. Sharma said the memory shortage will affect pricing and availability.
items.why: Gamers now have an official timeline for the next Xbox hardware.

tech-pulse.headline: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, its production inference engine, and it tops Hacker News with 2,179 points.
tech-pulse.note: GitHub Trending showed no AI or DevOps launches of note; Reddit top posts (via Composio) were mostly news, memes or opinion, and r/MachineLearning and r/devops had low engagement.

items.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, its production inference engine
items.body: DeepSeek released DeepInfer under the Apache 2.0 license. It powers DeepSeek's production services and supports DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on NVIDIA SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs. Features include MoE expert parallelism, DSpark speculative decoding, async scheduling and structured outputs. This release covers offline inference only, without KV cache system or prefill/decode disaggregation.
items.why: Teams that self-host large MoE models get a reference engine with expert parallelism and speculative decoding from a frontier lab.

items.title: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys exposed; browsers block certificates
items.body: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs were recoverable from the certificates because of bad key generation in April 2025. The issue was reported on 17 October. Firefox and Chrome blocked the certificates first, then Apple on 19 October and Microsoft on 20 October. Clients that do not check revocation or enforce Certificate Transparency need software updates.
items.why: Servers, containers and CI images that trust system CA bundles need updated trust stores to block forged TLS certificates.

items.title: Mistral launches Voxtral 3 speech models and voice agent SDK
items.body: Voxtral 3 includes transcription models for 50+ languages with diarization, a realtime model under 500 ms latency, and a TTS model for 35+ languages with voice cloning. The voice agent SDK is built on LiveKit and supports SIP, WebRTC and function calling. Batch transcription costs from $0.0035 per minute and the agent API from $0.04 per minute.
items.why: It gives a low-cost API option for transcription, text-to-speech and real-time voice agents with tool calling.

items.title: Cloudflare and VoidZero port the TypeScript compiler to Rust
items.body: Tsrs is an experimental Rust port of the TypeScript compiler, incubated in the Oxc toolchain with the TypeScript team. Cloudflare reports up to 8x faster checks and about 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0. Cloudflare says frontier AI models now make large ports possible in days. It is available with npm install tsrs.
items.why: Faster type checks cut CI time and make TypeScript tooling run in browsers through WebAssembly.

items.title: Google open-sources TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for TPUs
items.body: TorchTPU implements PyTorch ATen kernels for TPUs and integrates with torch.compile. It supports data and tensor parallelism and ships examples for Llama, Qwen and ResNet. Version 0.2.0 is on PyPI under the Apache 2.0 license.
items.why: PyTorch teams can train and serve models on Cloud TPUs without a rewrite to JAX.

aws-news.headline: Amazon Bedrock adds structured outputs for all Claude models, so apps get schema-valid JSON without custom parsing.

items.title: Bedrock adds structured outputs for all Claude models
items.body: Amazon Bedrock now supports structured outputs for all Anthropic Claude models. Responses conform to a JSON schema that the developer defines. The feature works on the bedrock-runtime endpoint through boto3 and on the bedrock-mantle endpoint through the Messages API. It is available in all Regions where Claude models are available.
items.why: Teams can drop custom JSON parsing and retry logic from Claude-based pipelines.

items.title: Bedrock Guardrails gets Standard tier for hallucination grounding checks
items.body: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails adds a Standard tier for contextual grounding checks. The Standard tier supports responses with reasoning or conversational content and has broader language support than the Classic tier. Pricing is the same for both tiers, and existing guardrails stay on Classic until you change them. The Standard tier requires cross-Region inference with a guardrail profile and is not listed for Mumbai or Hyderabad.
items.why: Grounding checks now work for conversational and reasoning answers, not only summaries, at the same price.

items.title: Bedrock Prompt Optimization can now shorten prompts to cut token cost
items.body: Amazon Bedrock Advanced Prompt Optimization adds an optional prompt shortening setting per prompt template. It returns an optimized prompt only when the prompt is shorter and scores at least as high on your evaluation. Results show a compression ratio and the original and optimized token counts. It works with steering criteria, LLM-as-a-judge rubrics and custom Lambda evaluators.
items.why: Shorter prompts lower input token cost and time to first token without a drop in quality.

items.title: Amazon ECS Gateway brings managed ingress for ECS services
items.body: Amazon ECS Gateway is a new managed ingress resource that provisions and manages Application Load Balancers in your account. Each service gets its own DNS hostname with host-based routing, and up to 25 services can share one ALB. ECS adds and removes ALBs as needed. It supports awsvpc services on all launch types in all commercial Regions, with no extra charge beyond the underlying resources.
items.why: Platform teams get shared, managed ALB ingress for ECS, with up to 25 services per load balancer.

items.title: IAM Identity Center keeps users when you move off Active Directory
items.body: AWS IAM Identity Center now retains users, groups, memberships, permission set assignments and application assignments when you change the identity source from Active Directory. Users and groups keep the same IDs, so policies that reference them keep working. The feature applies to organization instances in all Regions where the service is available. It has no additional cost.
items.why: Teams can move from Active Directory to Okta or Entra ID without rebuilding users and access assignments.

items.title: TorchNeuron public beta runs native PyTorch on AWS Trainium
items.body: AWS released TorchNeuron in public beta, an open source native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium. Code runs on Trainium by changing the device to .to('neuron'). It supports eager execution, torch.compile and the Neuron Kernel Interface for custom operators. It supports EC2 Trainium2 and Trainium3 instances.
items.why: Existing PyTorch code can move to Trainium chips with a one-line device change.

layoffs.headline: eBay cuts about 9% of staff, near 1,000 jobs, in its second round this year.
layoffs.note: Layoffs.fyi did not show its table; no new Indian IT or startup layoffs with a reliable source appeared in the last 48 hours.

items.title: eBay cuts 9% of workforce in second round this year
items.body: eBay will cut about 9% of its workforce, around 1,000 jobs, as first reported by Reuters with figures from Bloomberg. CEO Jamie Iannone's memo says eBay wants to simplify how it operates and move money to its fastest-growing areas. Teams and locations were not named. eBay cut about 800 jobs in February 2026.
items.why: It shows big e-commerce platforms keep shrinking staff to shift money into growth areas.
items.source: The Next Web, citing Reuters and Bloomberg

items.title: Qualcomm starts worldwide performance-based layoffs
items.body: An internal memo seen by Reuters shows Qualcomm will cut jobs worldwide after annual reviews. CEO Cristiano Amon wrote that the company had consistently fallen short of expectations and needs a stronger performance culture. Qualcomm did not give a number of jobs or name teams. Fiscal Q3 revenue fell 4% year on year to $9.95 billion.
items.why: Cuts at a major chip vendor signal pressure in the handset market that supplies edge AI hardware.
